hypotheses.text: The diagnostic sensitivity of full-field electroretinography for distinguishing CLN3-associated retinal degeneration from early-onset Stargardt disease (STGD1) at initial presentation depends on a composite electrophysiological criterion (either dark-adapted electronegative response OR complete response extinction) rather than the presence of an electronegative waveform alone.
hypotheses.rationale: Sakti et al. reported electronegative ERGs in 5 of 5 pediatric CLN3 patients, suggesting 100% sensitivity for an electronegative waveform, whereas Kuper et al. and Weleber showed that dark-adapted responses in CLN3 disease can present as either electronegative or completely absent/undetectable depending on disease stage at evaluation. If a clinician requires an electronegative waveform strictly, patients presenting with extinguished dark-adapted ERG will be misclassified as non-CLN3.

evidence.text: In CLN3 disease, dark-adapted (DA) full-field electroretinogram (ERG) responses were either absent or electronegative. In early-onset STGD1, DA ERG responses were generally unaffected. None of the STGD1 patients had an electronegative ERG.

evidence.text: In juvenile NCL patients, ERG shows undetectable rod-specific ERGs and an electronegative maximal response, with profound b-wave attenuation relative to a-wave.

source.title: Batten disease: features to facilitate early diagnosis
source.quote: The electroretinogram (ERG) findings in this series included undetectable rod specific ERGs, an electronegative maximal response, reduced and delayed cone flicker ERGs, reduction in the b:a ratio in the photopic single flash ERG, and an undetectable pattern ERG.

hypotheses.text: The electronegative ERG configuration in CLN3 retinopathy reflects a stage-dependent functional transmission failure at the photoreceptor-to-depolarizing bipolar cell synapse that precedes complete photoreceptor cell loss.
hypotheses.rationale: Weleber and Collins noted that early in juvenile CLN3 disease, a-waves are relatively spared while b-waves are disproportionately ablated, mimicking an inner retinal or synaptic signaling defect before outer nuclear layer collapse extinguishes both waveforms. Chen et al. showed an adult non-syndromic CLN3 patient whose ERG converted to electronegative over longitudinal follow-up, corroborating this stage-dependent phenomenon.

evidence.text: Patients with JNCL invariably showed severe to profound ERG abnormalities when first tested, with marked loss of a-wave amplitudes and even greater loss of b-wave amplitudes, creating electronegative configuration waveforms.

source.title: The dystrophic retina in multisystem disorders: the electroretinogram in neuronal ceroid lipofuscinoses
source.quote: Patients with JNCL invariably showed severe to profound ERG abnormalities when first tested, with essentially no rod-mediated activity and marked loss of a-wave amplitudes with even greater loss of b-wave amplitudes, creating electronegative configuration waveforms.

evidence.text: In a 50-year-old female presenting with non-syndromic CLN3 retinal dystrophy due to compound heterozygous variants, ERG responses progressively became electronegative over longitudinal follow-up.

source.title: Clinical and molecular characterization of non-syndromic retinal dystrophy due to c.175G>A mutation in ceroid lipofuscinosis neuronal 3 (CLN3)
source.quote: ERG responses became electronegative and patient's serum contained anti-retinal antibodies.

hypotheses.text: Dark-adapted full-field ERG abnormalities (electronegative or non-recordable waveforms) demonstrate 100% specificity in differentiating CLN3-associated maculopathy from early-onset STGD1 at presentation, despite imperfect sensitivity of the electronegative waveform when evaluated in isolation.
hypotheses.rationale: Kuper et al. explicitly proved that 0 of 20 early-onset STGD1 children demonstrated an electronegative or extinguished dark-adapted ERG at initial evaluation (dark-adapted responses were generally normal), whereas 100% of CLN3 patients had either electronegative or absent dark-adapted responses.

evidence.text: In early-onset STGD1, dark-adapted ERG responses were generally unaffected at presentation, and none of the 20 STGD1 patients showed an electronegative ERG, whereas all 18 CLN3 patients had either absent or electronegative dark-adapted responses.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact proportion of isolated RP101 (non-syndromic CLN3) patients that exhibit an electronegative ERG versus typical rod-cone dystrophy or extinguished ERG at first presentation across all published adult-onset cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: Most existing electronegative ERG studies evaluated pediatric CLN3 (Batten) cohorts rather than isolated RP101. Clarifying whether adult RP101 shows inner-retinal electronegativity or standard rod-cone attenuation will establish whether this sign discriminates RP101 from classic nonsyndromic RP.

new_directions.question_text: Does the presence of anti-retinal antibodies in adult-onset CLN3 retinopathy directly correlate with the emergence of an electronegative full-field ERG waveform?
new_directions.rationale: Chen et al. identified concurrent electronegative ERG transformation and anti-retinal antibodies in a non-syndromic CLN3 patient, suggesting secondary autoimmune or paraneoplastic-like inner retinal bipolar cell dysfunction rather than direct photoreceptor atrophy.
